terms.meaning: A curved mirror whose shiny surface curves inward, like the inside of a spoon.
A curved mirror whose shiny surface curves outward, like the back of a spoon.
A line at right angles to the mirror at the point where the ray hits it.
Transparent material with two surfaces, at least one of them curved.
A lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges.
A lens that is thinner in the middle than at the edges.

items.name: Image in a concave mirror
items.formula: Close up: erect and enlarged. Farther away: inverted.
items.example: Your face looks big and upright when close to it.

items.name: Image in a convex mirror
items.example: A car behind you looks small but upright.

items.name: Uses of concave mirrors
items.formula: Torches, vehicle headlights, dentists’ mirrors and solar concentrators.
items.example: A dentist sees an enlarged image of a tooth.

items.name: Uses of convex mirrors
items.formula: Vehicle side mirrors and mirrors at sharp bends, because they show a wide area.
items.example: A mirror at a blind turn shows oncoming traffic.

items.name: First law of reflection
items.formula: Angle of incidence = Angle of reflection
items.example: A ray hits at 35° to the normal, so it leaves at 35° to the normal.

items.name: Second law of reflection
items.formula: The incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
items.example: They can all be drawn on one sheet of paper.

items.name: Where the laws apply
items.formula: The laws hold for all mirrors: plane, concave and convex.
items.example: Curved mirrors still obey them at each point.

items.name: Beam of light on mirrors
items.formula: A concave mirror converges parallel rays. A convex mirror spreads them out.
items.example: A concave mirror can focus sunlight on paper to burn it.

items.name: Image in a convex lens
items.formula: Close to the object: erect and enlarged. Far away: inverted.
items.example: This is how a magnifying glass works.

items.name: Image in a concave lens
items.example: Objects look small through it wherever they are.

items.name: Beam of light through lenses
items.formula: A convex lens converges rays. A concave lens spreads them out.
items.example: A convex lens makes a bright spot of sunlight.

items.name: Uses of lenses
items.example: The eye has a natural convex lens.

mistakes.text: Measure the angles from the normal, not from the mirror’s surface.
A concave mirror converges light, but so does a convex lens. Do not match them by name.
A convex mirror’s image is never enlarged, wherever the object is.
